The challenge encourages innovation using real NASA datasets.

Users can search for astronomical objects, access available observations, view scientific FITS images, and compare images captured at different times using an interactive Cosmic Time Machine and Cosmic Blink Viewer.

The platform also aims to help users investigate possible moving objects, brightness variations, and spectral information through image comparison and scientific analysis tools. It combines astronomy data processing with interactive visualizations to make complex scientific information more accessible.

COSMIC LENS addresses the challenge by transforming astronomical observations into an engaging exploration experience for students, researchers, and space enthusiasts. It encourages curiosity, supports science education, and promotes citizen-science participation. Its goal is to make the changing infrared universe easier to explore while helping users investigate interesting astronomical events using real scientific data.
details:
COSMIC LENS – SPHEREx Sky Explorer

COSMIC LENS is an interactive astronomy platform designed to make the infrared universe easier to explore using NASA's SPHEREx mission data. It allows users to search astronomical objects using their coordinates (Right Ascension and Declination), retrieve available observations, view infrared images, and investigate how celestial objects and their surroundings change over time.

The platform processes scientific FITS files using astronomy tools and converts them into understandable visualizations. Its features include a FITS Image Viewer, Cosmic Time Machine, and a WiseView-inspired Cosmic Blink Viewer that allows users to switch between observations from different dates. Users can also compare images through difference imaging, investigate possible moving objects using source detection and motion analysis, explore SPHEREx's 102-channel spectral information, and study brightness variations when suitable data is available. A Citizen Science Discovery Hub is designed to help users explore and report potential astronomical candidates.

The main benefit of COSMIC LENS is that it brings complex astronomical data and multiple exploration tools together in one accessible platform. It helps students, astronomy enthusiasts, and researchers understand infrared observations without needing to work directly with complicated scientific files. It also encourages curiosity, scientific learning, and participation in astronomical research.

The intended impact is to make space science more accessible, encourage citizen-science participation, and provide an interactive way to investigate the changing universe. By combining real astronomical observations with image visualization and scientific analysis, COSMIC LENS aims to help users identify interesting changes and possible astronomical candidates that may deserve further investigation.

The project is being developed using React.js and Vite for the frontend, Python and FastAPI for the backend, and Tailwind CSS for the user interface. Scientific data processing uses libraries such as Astropy, Astroquery, NumPy, SciPy, Photutils, and Reproject. Plotly.js is used for scientific charts, while Aladin Lite supports interactive sky visualization. Three.js and Framer Motion are intended for advanced visual effects and animations. SQLite is used for initial data management, with PostgreSQL as a possible future option. The main data source is the NASA/IPAC SPHEREx archive.

What makes COSMIC LENS creative is its combination of astronomical science and an interactive visual experience. Inspired by time-based infrared viewers such as WiseView, it introduces a blinking observation experience, image comparison, candidate tracking, spectral exploration, and motion-aligned image stacking in one platform. Its cinematic space-themed interface makes scientific exploration engaging while keeping the underlying measurements and observations scientifically grounded.

During development, our team considered scientific accuracy, real NASA data availability, image quality, coordinate accuracy, observation dates, FITS file processing, measurement uncertainty, usability, accessibility, performance, and the limitations of astronomical observations. We also considered that not every target will have enough observations for motion, spectral, or brightness analysis. Therefore, the platform is designed to distinguish actual measurements from possible candidates and clearly report when data is unavailable.

Our vision is to make the changing infrared universe easier for everyone to explore: Explore the Changing Universe. Discover What Others Cannot See.
